steps: On your router, keep TCP port 443 going to your front door (192.168.1.20), and send UDP port 443 to this server (192.168.1.212) for call audio.

guides.title: Pangolin
guides.note: Pangolin's Resources page can't do this: it passes raw TCP on by port, not by name, so Linx would need a port of its own. This goes in Traefik's settings file instead, next to Pangolin's own, and Pangolin's sites keep working as before.
steps: On the Pangolin machine (192.168.1.20), open config/traefik/dynamic_config.yml.
If it has no line that is exactly “tcp:”, add the block below to the end of the file.

If it has one, don't add a second (Traefik would ignore the whole file): put the block's “routers:” and “services:” entries under the existing “tcp:”, and its “linx-proxy-protocol” lines under the existing “serversTransports:”, keeping Pangolin's own entries. Another Linx's entries stay: this one's are named linx-example-com-….
Traefik picks it up by itself within a few seconds. To see that it took it: docker logs traefik --since 1m 2>&1 | grep -i error should say nothing about dynamic_config.yml.

Recommended: in traefik_config.yml, remove the “http3:” lines (and “advertisedPort: 443” under them) from the websecure entry point, then docker restart traefik. Otherwise browsers visiting your other Pangolin sites try UDP 443, which now goes to Linx, and wait a moment before falling back.

files.title: the block for Pangolin
files.text:
# Linx at example.com, passed through Pangolin's Traefik (docs/WEB.md §3). Generated by linx setup.
# Add this to Pangolin's config/traefik/dynamic_config.yml (see FRONT-DOOR.txt:
# if that file already has a "tcp:" line, merge into it; never add a second).
# Traefik picks it up by itself; nothing needs restarting.
tcp:
  routers:
    linx-example-com-web:
      entryPoints: [websecure]
      rule: "HostSNI(`example.com`)"
      tls:
        passthrough: true
      service: linx-example-com-web
    linx-example-com-turn:
      entryPoints: [websecure]
      rule: "HostSNI(`turn.example.com`)"
      tls:
        passthrough: true
      service: linx-example-com-turn
  services:
    linx-example-com-web:
      loadBalancer:
        serversTransport: linx-proxy-protocol
        servers:
          - address: "192.168.1.212:8443"
    linx-example-com-turn:
      loadBalancer:
        servers:
          - address: "192.168.1.212:5349"
  serversTransports:
    linx-proxy-protocol:
      proxyProtocol:
        version: 2

guides.title: nginx
guides.note: nginx needs its stream module (it's in nginx.org's and Debian's packages). The block takes over port 443 and passes your own websites on to them.
steps: Add the block below to nginx.conf at the top level (next to “http {”, not inside it).

In each of your own sites' “server” blocks that has “listen 443 ssl”, change that line to “listen 127.0.0.1:4443 ssl proxy_protocol;” and add “set_real_ip_from 127.0.0.1;” and “real_ip_header proxy_protocol;”. Your sites keep their visitors' real addresses.
sudo nginx -t && sudo systemctl reload nginx

files.title: the block for nginx

guides.title: HAProxy
steps: In your frontend on port 443 (mode tcp, with “tcp-request inspect-delay 5s” and “tcp-request content accept if { req_ssl_hello_type 1 }”), add the two use_backend lines from the block's comments above your other use_backend lines.
Add the two backends from the block, then reload HAProxy.

files.title: the block for HAProxy
files.text:
# Linx, passed through HAProxy by name (docs/WEB.md §3). Generated by linx setup.
# In your HAProxy frontend on port 443 (mode tcp, with
#   tcp-request inspect-delay 5s
#   tcp-request content accept if { req_ssl_hello_type 1 }
# ) add these two lines above your other use_backend lines:
#   use_backend linx_web if { req_ssl_sni -i example.com }
#   use_backend linx_turn if { req_ssl_sni -i turn.example.com }
# and add these backends:

backend linx_web
    mode tcp
    server linx 192.168.1.212:8443 send-proxy-v2

backend linx_turn
    mode tcp
    server linx 192.168.1.212:5349

guides.note: Caddy needs its layer-4 add-on (github.com/mholt/caddy-l4) to pass Linx through: download Caddy with the “layer4” package from caddyserver.com/download, or build it with xcaddy. Your own sites keep working as before.
steps: Add the block below to the top of your Caddyfile. If it already starts with a “{ … }” block, put the “servers { … }” part inside that one instead of adding a second.

guides.title: Nginx Proxy Manager
guides.note: Nginx Proxy Manager can only pass traffic through by port, not by name, so this works only if nothing else needs port 443.
steps: If nothing else needs port 443: have your router send TCP and UDP port 443 straight to this server, and choose “Nothing else uses port 443 — Linx takes it” instead.

If your other sites need port 443 too: Caddy (with its layer-4 add-on), nginx or HAProxy can pass Linx through by name next to them. As a last resort, Advanced has “My proxy must unlock the traffic itself”, which works with Nginx Proxy Manager as it is.

guides.title: A router or firewall
guides.note: A router or firewall passes traffic through by port, not by name, so it can send port 443 to one machine only.
steps: If nothing else needs port 443, forward TCP and UDP port 443 to this server (192.168.1.212) and choose “Nothing else uses port 443 — Linx takes it” instead.
If another program needs it, keep port 443 going to that program and follow its tab here.
